name: Generate a Semantic-Layer Data Product from a Schema

checks.check: models.py declares the physical semantic_model("customer_profile") and semantic_model("order_event") objects. CUSTOMER_ID and ORDER_ID are declared with the public field(..., primary_key(), dimension(...)) DSL, and both semantic_model objects have non-empty .description(...) text.

A public metric_field(metric(...)) on a semantic_view declares total_revenue with Agg.SUM over order_event.field("AMOUNT_USD") and order_count with Agg.COUNT_DISTINCT over order_event.field("ORDER_ID"). Metrics must use the public DSL, not a hand-written SemanticRegistry.

The churned-customer-count metric over customer_profile.field("IS_CHURNED") and the first-order-count metric over order_event.field("IS_FIRST_ORDER") use Agg.SUM with boolean=True in their public metric(...) calls, so the compiler emits a boolean CASE-sum rather than a numeric cast.
The order_event CUSTOMER_ID attribute carries the public field(..., join(to="customer_profile", to_column="CUSTOMER_ID")) role. The join is declared on the many-side order_event model.
In the public field(..., dimension(...)) roles, EMAIL and FULL_NAME set pii=True, and no other dimension is marked PII. The exhaustive half is graded from the complete models.py workspace file.

spec.py exposes the MCP tools via a single .semantic_tools(service=...) call. It does NOT hand-wire build_semantic_tools + rpc_function + rpc_server, and does NOT call data_product_rpc_output() directly (that raises ValidationError alongside .semantic_tools()).

spec.py promises the physical customer_profile and order_event models on a plain storage(...) port via data_product_output().promise(...), registers every query-time semantic_view that carries metrics, and does not configure the storage port with as_view(...).

transform.py seeds the base tables (CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE + write_pandas) and is wired via .transform(code(transform)...). There is NO @on_provision hook, NO .provision(...) call, and NO semantic-view (CREATE VIEW / SEMANTIC VIEW) DDL anywhere.

The agent does NOT re-implement or vendor the compiler / tool factory (no hand-written compile_selection, filter, or aggregation logic, no copied nxd.experimental.semantic source). The tools are auto-generated by the .semantic_tools() flag from the installed wheel.
The project's dependency file lists nxd.data_product[spec], nxd.drivers[rpc], snowflake-connector-python[pandas], pandas, and pyyaml (>=6.0.2) for the split-pod manifest fallback.

Every declared dimension and metric carries a non-empty description inside its public dimension(description=...) or metric(description=...) role, stating what the concept is and the population it covers, and each semantic_model declares a description. A description on the enclosing field(...) or metric_field(...) is not sufficient because it does not reach describe_model.
